narrative: The analysis processed 228 working days of demand data for PL3__M9CD9474 with 3 outliers winsorised at 901.45 units. Demand exhibits a lumpy pattern with a heavy-tailed distribution (CV=1.48) and a mean of 147.61 units/day on 71.1% of active days, with no significant trend. Lead times are unstable (mean=1.58 days, CV=0.83), necessitating a conservative effective lead time of 2.24 days. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 4,680 units and a 553-unit safety stock is recommended, achieving 95% service level at an estimated annual total cost of $887.54 — a 39.5% reduction versus the SAP baseline of $1,467.46 — while consuming only 38.6% of available storage capacity.
warnings: High demand variability detected (CV=1.48). Consider robust methods.
Unstable lead time detected (CV=0.83). Monitor supplier performance.

research_insights.selected_model: Continuous-review (r,Q) with EOQ order quantity and Normal-approximation safety stock
research_insights.selection_rationale: The lumpy, high-CV demand profile combined with unstable lead times requires an explicit safety stock buffer. The (r,Q) policy with EOQ balances the low unit cost ($1.40) against the fixed ordering cost ($50), and the Normal approximation at z=1.645 provides the target 95% service level. The robust SS (351 units) is offered as a lower bound given the heavy-tailed distribution risk.
research_insights.boundary_risk: CV=1.48 indicates heavy-tailed demand distribution; Normal approximation may understate tail risk and actual stockout frequency could exceed 5% during demand spikes. The robust safety stock of 351 units is the minimum defensible buffer.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (1394) + safety stock (553) = 1947 units, well within max_storage_units (13557). No infeasibility detected.
